verdict: IMPLEMENTED, NOT MEASURED. The three clauses rehearsal 3 left open are ruled on and built, test-first, with core `make ci` + integration on a fresh native PostgreSQL and every GitHub lane green. INT-05 does NOT move: nothing here was run against a second Vidra, and only the fourth two-instance run can flip it.
section: A29 follow-ups — a block that speaks, resumed comments, validator-safe renames — 2026-09-09
headline: An instance block now answers a Follow with a signed Reject (and nothing else); comment Creates cancelled inside a block window resume on unblock when the comment is still readable; migration 0143 mints renamed channel handles in the channel-handle validator's own alphabet and re-renames what 0142 already minted, keeping the frozen ActivityPub id where it is.
ruling: An instance block SPEAKS: a Follow refused because the sender's instance is blocked is answered with a signed Reject, the same shape a creator's manual rejection sends, so the sender ends `rejected` rather than stranded at `pending`. Notes and other activities from a blocked instance stay 202-and-dropped with the audit row, and produce no other outbound speech.
Cancelled comment Creates resume on unblock when the comment still exists, is not hidden, and its video is still public+published on an AP-enabled channel; anything else stays cancelled.

The backfill uses the channel-handle validator's alphabet: `<handle>_channel`, `<handle>_channel2`, … Existing `-channel[-N]` renames minted by 0142 get a second audited rename to the underscore form with the same alias treatment; the frozen AP id does not move.

sc1_a_block_that_speaks.verdict: PASS by test (unit + drain-to-a-real-inbox); UNVERIFIED live
sc1_a_block_that_speaks.shape_is_shared: buildRejectFollow — the same function RejectFollowerRequest (a creator's manual rejection) and the federation_allow_channel_followers gate already use. A sender must not have to recognise two kinds of refusal.
sc1_a_block_that_speaks.signed_as: the channel actor, at the id this instance PUBLISHES (the FROZEN one for a renamed channel, via channelActorHandle) — vidra has no instance-level AP actor, and an Accept and a Reject for one channel must not be signed by two actors.
sc1_a_block_that_speaks.wire_answer_unchanged: 202, plus one audit row federation.inbox.rejected carrying only the domain. The activity is NOT marked processed, so an unblock still lets a redelivery in.

Follow whose actor is not the request signer

Follow of a channel with activitypub_enabled false (0096)

cancellation_exemption.mechanism: severingActivity() already returns true for Undo and Reject (A29-F5), so DrainDeliveries does not cancel them for a blocked destination. VERIFIED AND KEPT.
cancellation_exemption.how_it_is_proved: TestTheBlocksOwnRejectIsDeliveredWhileTheBlockStands drives the whole path: the Follow arrives from a blocked domain, the sender's inbox is an httptest server whose host is ALSO on the blocklist, DrainDeliveries returns delivered=1, no row carries the cancel marker, and the Reject is read back off the wire naming the refused Follow.
cancellation_exemption.not_asserted_by: re-reading severingActivity, which would prove only that the predicate agrees with itself

sc1_a_block_that_speaks.sender_side: TestAnInstanceBlocksRejectEndsTheSendersRow builds the Reject with the BLOCKING instance's own buildRejectFollow and feeds it to the sender's inbox: the row goes `rejected` (terminal, creator-visible), and a re-follow re-arms it to `pending` with a NEW Follow activity id. The sender learns nothing about the block.
sc1_a_block_that_speaks.best_effort: rejectFollowFromBlockedSender returns nothing and logs on failure. HandleInbox must answer ErrSenderBlocked (202 + audit row) whatever happens, because a queue error that propagated would turn the refusal into a 422 — exactly the distinguishable answer the silence exists to avoid.

sc2_comment_creates_resume.verdict: PASS by unit test AND by a fresh-Postgres integration test; UNVERIFIED live
sc2_comment_creates_resume.what_was_broken: redeliverable() resolved a Create/Update's object only as <base>/videos/<uuid>. A comment's object id is <base>/comments/<uuid>, so a Create{Note} cancelled inside a block window fell to the conservative default and was left cancelled forever — a follower's mirrored thread permanently short every comment written while the block stood.

resume_predicate.resumed: the comment row still exists AND deleted_at IS NULL AND user_id IS NOT NULL (locally authored) AND its video is privacy='public' AND state='published' AND its channel has activitypub_enabled
left_cancelled: the comment is gone — a removal is a hard DELETE, so the row is simply not found; sending the Create would plant a comment this instance can no longer retract, because the Delete that would retract it was cancelled by the same block and no longer resolves
the comment is tombstoned (deleted_at set by an account deletion, body emptied, row kept so the thread survives) — broadcasting the original body would un-delete it on someone else's server
the comment is remote-authored — federateComment never fans those out, and a resume path that did would be a re-broadcast by the back door
the video is no longer public+published on an AP-enabled channel — same clause, same helper as the video arm
the Note id belongs to another instance
resume_predicate.deliberately_not_consulted: per-viewer blocks and mutes. Those are read filters evaluated against ONE reader, and a fan-out to a remote inbox has no reader to evaluate them for; the receiving instance applies its own readers' filters to what it stores. The only instance-wide hiding a local comment has is deletion (hard) or tombstoning, and both are refused above.

sc2_comment_creates_resume.bounds: cap, window and domain prefilter are the VIDEO path's, unchanged, because it is the same loop: ListCancelledDeliveriesForRedelivery with the LIKE prefilter, maxRedeliverAfterUnblock = 500 applied after it, and hostOf() deciding membership with the same function that decided to cancel.
tests: internal/federation/a29_follow_ups_test.go: TestUnblockRequeuesCancelledCommentCreates — through the real DrainDeliveries cancellation and the real RedeliverAfterUnblock

internal/federation/a29_follow_ups_integration_test.go: TestUnblockResumesCommentCreatesForVisibleComments — seeded rows on a REAL PostgreSQL: 4 queued Create{Note}s, real BlockInstance, real drain, real unblock; requeued=1 and the other three keep the cancel marker intact

sc3_migration_0143.verdict: PASS by integration test on a real PostgreSQL, including a full up/down/up cycle with seeded rows
sc3_migration_0143.rule: mint_channel_handle(base): fold the source handle to [A-Za-z0-9_], keep the whole name inside the validator's 30-character ceiling by truncating the ROOT (not the suffix), and mint <root>_channel, then <root>_channel2, <root>_channel3, … with NO separator before the number. The 3-character floor takes care of itself because '_channel' is 8 characters.
sc3_migration_0143.why_truncate_the_root: a name that came out as <31 chars>_channel would be refused by the validator exactly as a hyphen is; truncating the suffix instead would collapse _channel2 back onto _channel and lose the loop's purpose.

second_rename.detection: a channel holding an is_actor_id alias (only 0142's backfill mints one) whose CURRENT handle still matches '-channel(-[0-9]+)?$'. Both clauses matter: the first keeps a channel a human deliberately called my-channel out of it, the second keeps the migration off channels a later validator-clean rename already fixed.
second_rename.frozen_actor_id: NOT MOVED. 0142 froze it on the ORIGINAL colliding name and peers hold that id in their follow rows, their cached actors and every activity's attributedTo. 0143 does not touch the is_actor_id alias.
second_rename.interim_name: becomes an ORDINARY second alias — is_actor_id=false, expires_at now + 365 days — so anyone who published the interim name in the window between two upgrades gets a 301 rather than a 404.
second_rename.audit: content.channel.handle_renamed, again, with reason 'from=<interim> to=<new>' and metadata {from, to, original, cause: 'handle_validator_alphabet'}

sc3_migration_0143.down_reverses_only_0143: restores the interim handles, deletes the aliases 0143 minted, deletes the audit rows carrying cause=handle_validator_alphabet (a ledger must not describe a rename that has been reversed — the rows are identified exactly, by one cause written by one function), drops mint_channel_handle and rename_channel_handles_to_validator_alphabet, and restores 0142's backfill verbatim.

sc4_docs_and_operator_surfaces.core_docs: vidra-core docs/operations.md gains '## Federation — what an instance block does, and what an unblock undoes': inbound is gone for good (202, dropped, audit row), the ONE inbound activity that gets an answer, outbound is held not lost with lazy cancellation, a table separating dead_lettered from cancelled_by_policy, the resume list, the percent-encoded unblock path, and a '### Channel handles the one-namespace migration renamed' subsection with the SQL to find out whether any of yours were renamed and what to tell those creators.

admin_system.was: count(*) FILTER (WHERE state = 'failed') AS dead_lettered — which included block-cancelled rows and reported them as 'N outbound deliveries exhausted their retries and were dead-lettered. The instance is serving; one or more peers did not accept what it sent.' The rehearsal watched six cancelled deliveries reported that way.
admin_system.now: FederationDeliveryHealth takes the cancel marker as a parameter (from internal/federation.DeliveryCancelledByPolicy, so the string lives once next to the code that writes it) and splits: dead_lettered EXCLUDES cancelled rows, cancelled_by_policy counts them.
admin_system.status: cancellations alone do NOT degrade the component — a blocklist doing what an admin asked for is not a degradation, and a page that went yellow for it would train operators to ignore yellow. The count rides in detail and is ABSENT when zero.

user_label.finding: rehearsal 3, Chromium: the control's accessible name was 'Block films@peer.example' — the CHANNEL handle — on a control that sends /accounts/creatora and blocks the PERSON who owns it. Recorded there as 'a wording gap worth closing, not a behaviour one'.
user_label.fix: the accessible name follows the URL the page is about to send: 'Block account kaisa@peer.example' when the row carries account_actor_url, and 'Block account films@peer.example' in the fallback case where the block genuinely IS against the channel actor. So the label tells the truth in both directions.
user_label.behaviour: unchanged — same URL blocked, same URL unblocked, same visible button text ('Block account' / 'Unblock account', which it already said).
